notes: keda implies a finished action, so it cannot always replace ser or wordo (Nota 1, p. 38).
keda can also be an independent verb, a passive auxiliary or a copulative verb (Nota 1, p. 38).
ta is also the present tense/aspect particle (particles.tsv). Write Ta logico cu ..., not E ta logico cu ... (Nota 3, p. 39).
As a copulative verb it is followed by a proper name and takes no ta: Mi ruman yama Alfredo (Nota 2, p. 39).
